'''Robert E. Maizell''' (1924–2007) was an American [[chemical information]] scholar who served at the [[American Institute of Physics]] as a director of a research project which focused on communication between scientists. Maizell also served as the head of the research library at [[Olin Mathieson Chemical]].

== Early life and education ==
Robert Edward Maizell was born in 1924 in [[Baltimore, Maryland]]. In 1945, he earned his Bachelor of Science in [[chemistry]] from [[Loyola University Maryland]]. In 1951, Maizell joined the [[American Chemical Society]]. Maizell won a scholarship to [[Columbia University]] for his master's program for the 1948–1949 academic year, and by 1957, he had a Bachelor of Science, Master of Science, and a PhD in [[Library Science]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Ainsworth |first=Susan J. |date=11 February 2008 |title=Obituaries |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/86/i6/Obituaries.html |access-date=10 April 2026 |website=Chemical & Engineering News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Service |first=Columbia University School of Library |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Report/_3MVAAAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Maizell&pg=RA20-PA9&printsec=frontcover |title=Report |date=1927 |language=en}}</ref>

== Career and academic work ==
Maizell worked with [[Mathieson Chemical]] in [[Niagara Falls, New York]], and eventually relocated to [[New Haven, Connecticut]] once Mathieson Chemical merged with [[Olin Corporation]]. There, Maizell worked as a business manager and was also in charge of the research library. He remained with them until he retired in 1986.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=11 December 1958 |title=PHYSICS POST FILLED; Institute Names Director in Communications Study |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1958/12/11/archives/physics-post-filled-institute-names-director-in-communications.html |access-date=10 April 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> In 1958, Maizell was also offered a position with the [[American Institute of Physics]] which was funded by the [[National Science Foundation]] and the [[United States Atomic Energy Commission|Atomic Energy Commission]]. At the American Institute of Physics, Maizell worked as the director of a research project on [[Documentation science|documentation]] and communication in physics.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

Maizell published academic papers in relation to his work. In 1960, he published the paper ''"''Information Gathering Patterns and Creativity A Study of Research Chemists in an Industrial Research Laboratory''".'' This paper was featured in [[American Documentation]] and focused on how creativity can lead to chemists to read more specialized papers, cite older sources, and think more broadly than their "non-creative" counterparts.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Maizell |first=Robert E. |date=January 1960 |title=Information gathering patterns and creativity a study of research chemists in an industrial research laboratory |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/asi.5090110104 |journal=American Documentation |language=en |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=9–17 |doi=10.1002/asi.5090110104 |issn=0096-946X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Additionally, he also published "International Conference for Standards on a Common Language for Machine Searching Translation<nowiki>''</nowiki> in 1960. This short paper focused on whether or not librarians should be invited to conferences that focus on mechanical information retrieval and how they may benefit the field.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Maizell |first=Robert E. |date=3 January 1960 |title=International Conference for Standards on a Common Language for Machine Searching Translation |url=http://crl.acrl.org/index.php/crl/article/view/11305 |journal=College & Research Libraries |volume=21 |issue=2 |pages=125–126 |doi=10.5860/crl_21_02_25 |issn=2150-6701|hdl=2142/37268 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> In 1979, he published the first edition of his book ''How to Find Chemical Information: A Guide for Practicing Chemists, Teachers, and Students''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Maizell |first=Robert E. |date=January 1980 |title=How to Find Chemical Information: A Guide for Practicing Chemists, Teachers, and Students. Robert E. Maizell |url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/601068 |journal=The Library Quarterly |volume=51 |issue=1 |pages=121–122 |doi=10.1086/601068 |issn=0024-2519|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His book focuses on approach techniques and various tools for selecting chemical information and its retrieval.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 April 2026 |title=How to Find Chemical Information: A Guide for Practicing Chemists, Educators, and Students |url=https://www.barnesandnoble.com/w/how-to-find-chemical-information-robert-e-maizell/1101193184 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240511075102/https://www.barnesandnoble.com/w/how-to-find-chemical-information-robert-e-maizell/1101193184 |archive-date=May 11, 2024 |access-date=11 April 2026 |website=Barnes & Noble}}</ref> Since then, he has published three versions of ''How to Find Chemical Information'' and was working on a fourth version up until his death.<ref name=":0" />

Maizell was involved with the [[American Chemical Society]], initially becoming a member in 1951. He was a part of the Division of Chemical Literature and its successor, the Division of Chemical Information.<ref name=":0" /> In 1968, he was appointed as a liaison representative from the [[American Society of Information Science & Technology|American Society of Information Science]] and in 1971, was elected as chairman of the division.<ref name=":2">“The American Chemical Society.” Stanford University Libraries. Accessed 11 April 2026. <nowiki>https://web.stanford.edu/group/swain/cinf/50years/cinf50th_all.pdf</nowiki>.</ref> In 1975, Maizell was appointed as the Computer Program Complications and Technological Forecasting committee chairman, and was the alternate councilor for the Division of Chemical Information in 1976 and 1977.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Section 4: 50 Years of Chemical Information in the ACS 1943–1993: ACS Division of Chemical Information: Projects and hosted sites archive: Swain Library |url=https://web.stanford.edu/group/swain/cinf/50years/cinf50th_3.html |access-date=11 April 2026 |website=web.stanford.edu}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

Maizell founded Technology Information Consultants, a consulting firm located in [[New Haven, Connecticut]], as a retirement project. His firm focused on chemical information retrieval, specifically with patents, on a global scale.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life and death ==
Maizell was married to his wife, Mona, with whom he had two children.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-12-07 |title=Mona Maizell Obituary {{!}} December 5, 2013 |url=https://www.courant.com/obituaries/mona-v-maizell-avon-ct/ |access-date=11 April 2026 |website=Hartford Courant |language=en-US}}</ref> He died on April 8, 2007 at age 82.<ref name=":0" />
